chunks: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام said: 'Indeed, menstruation for women is an impurity with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, afflicted them.

In the time of Nuh عليه السلام, women used to menstruate only once in the year, until some women came out from their dwellings, and they were seven hundred women. They went out, wore safflower-dyed garments, adorned themselves, and applied perfume. Then they went out and spread through the lands, sat with men, attended the festivals with them, and sat in their rows.

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, afflicted them at that point with menstruation every month—meaning those very women specifically. Their blood flowed, and they were removed from among the men. Thus they menstruated once every month, and Allah, Exalted is He, occupied them with menstruation and diminished their desire.' He said: 'As for other women, those who had not done what they had done, they would menstruate once every year.'

He said: 'Then the sons of those who menstruated every month married the daughters of those who menstruated once every year, and the people became intermixed. Then the daughters of these and those menstruated once every month. So the children of those who menstruated once every [month] became many due to the regularity of menstruation, while the children of those who menstruated once every year were few due to the فساد of the blood.'
He said: 'So the offspring of these increased, while the offspring of those decreased.'

key_terms.الْحَيْضَ: menstruation; the recurring bleeding discussed in the report
key_terms.شَهْوَتَهُنَّ: their desire, which the report says was diminished
key_terms.فَسادِ الدَّمِ: corruption of the blood, given here as the reason for fewer children
key_terms.نَجاسَةٌ: ritual impurity in the context of menstrual blood
key_terms.نُوحٍ: Nuh (Noah) عليه السلام, during whose time the narrated events are said to have occurred

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام describe the origin of monthly menstruation in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a narrative explanation of the origin of frequent menstruation among women, tracing it back to a group of women in the time of Nuh عليه السلام and describing how this condition later spread through intermarriage. It also connects menstruation to ritual impurity and places the report within the broader discussion of ghusl for menstruation.
